ar-19cb43e5.stem: What type of joint are the facet (zygapophysial) joints between the vertebrae?
ar-19cb43e5.explanation: The facet joints between the superior and inferior articular processes are plane joints that allow gliding; the orientation of their surfaces determines the range of movement of each region (oblique in the neck, coronal in the thorax, sagittal in the lumbar spine). Their degeneration is a common cause of low back pain.

ar-7888f307.stem: In what order do movements occur at the temporomandibular joint when the mouth opens?
options: The condyle stays fixed behind the articular tubercle
The disc glides backwards independently of the condyle
First gliding in the upper compartment, then rotation in the lower compartment
First the condyle rotates like a hinge in the lower compartment, then the condyle and disc glide forwards together in the upper compartment
ar-7888f307.explanation: The articular disc divides the TMJ into an upper (disc–fossa/tubercle) and a lower (disc–condyle) compartment. At the start of opening rotation occurs in the lower compartment; in wide opening the condyle–disc complex glides forwards towards the articular tubercle in the upper compartment (translation), driven by lateral pterygoid.

ar-9f52e25c.stem: With what tissue are the articular surfaces of the temporomandibular joint covered?
ar-9f52e25c.explanation: The TMJ is an atypical synovial joint whose articular surfaces are covered with fibrocartilage, not hyaline cartilage; this relates to the intramembranous origin of the mandible. The joints at both ends of the clavicle show the same feature.

ar-fd55eb81.stem: Which is the weakest part of the glenohumeral joint, and why?
options: The inferior part; there is no rotator cuff muscle or strong ligament support there
The anterior part; subscapularis is not present there
The superior part; there is no acromial support
The posterior part; the capsule is thinnest there
ar-fd55eb81.explanation: The rotator cuff wraps the capsule above, in front and behind; the inferior part is protected only by the lax capsule and the inferior glenohumeral ligament. In abduction the humeral head escapes downwards and forwards through this area, putting the axillary nerve at risk.

ar-0145e5e7.stem: What are the two parts of the coracoclavicular ligament?
ar-0145e5e7.explanation: The coracoclavicular ligament is the strongest ligament suspending the clavicle from the scapula: it has a medial conoid part (to the conoid tubercle) and a lateral trapezoid part (to the trapezoid line). If it also tears in an AC dislocation, the clavicle rises markedly.

ar-2ce80442.stem: Which statement about the sternoclavicular joint is true?
options: It is a ball-and-socket joint without a disc
It is a uniaxial hinge joint
It is a saddle-type synovial joint containing an articular disc
ar-2ce80442.explanation: The sternoclavicular joint is the only true joint connecting the upper limb to the trunk; its articular disc divides it in two and acts as a strong cushion preventing the clavicle sliding medially. The costoclavicular ligament is the joint's main stabiliser.

ar-b6f1b5ff.stem: Where is the triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC) located?
options: At the carpometacarpal joint of the thumb
Between the radius and the scaphoid
Between the distal end of the ulna and the lunate and triquetrum
ar-b6f1b5ff.explanation: The TFCC separates the ulnar head from the carpal bones, is the main stabiliser of the distal radio-ulnar joint and carries part of the load on the wrist. It can tear in a fall on the hand or with strain in ulnar deviation, causing pain on the ulnar side of the wrist.

ar-9c0521bf.stem: Why is radial deviation (abduction) of the wrist more limited than ulnar deviation?
options: The ulna is longer than the radius
The radial styloid process extends further down
The TFCC is on the radial side
The ulnar collateral ligament of the wrist is weak
ar-9c0521bf.explanation: The radial styloid process ends about 1 cm lower than the ulnar styloid and limits radial deviation by striking the scaphoid. Because the ulna does not articulate directly with the carpal bones, ulnar deviation is wider.

ar-24504957.stem: What type of joint are the proximal and distal radio-ulnar joints?
ar-24504957.explanation: Proximally the radial head rotates within the anular ligament, and distally the radius rotates around the ulnar head; together the two joints produce pronation and supination. The interosseous membrane between them is a syndesmosis.

ar-7abbb713.stem: What function does the direction of the fibres of the forearm interosseous membrane serve?
options: It transfers load from the hand and radius to the ulna
It transfers load from the ulna and radius to the hand
It replaces the collateral ligaments of the elbow
It only provides an origin for muscles
ar-7abbb713.explanation: At the wrist most of the load passes to the radius, at the elbow to the ulna (humero-ulnar joint). Because the membrane fibres run downwards and medially from the radius to the ulna, they transfer load from the radius to the ulna and provide a broad surface of origin for muscles.

ar-801c39ac.stem: What type of joint is the knee?
ar-801c39ac.explanation: The knee is a bicondylar joint between the two femoral condyles and the tibial plateaus that, in addition to hinge movement, allows some rotation in flexion; the patellofemoral joint lies within the same capsule.

ar-8ffbb6ae.stem: Which movement does the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) mainly prevent?
options: Forward slide of the tibia on the femur
Backward slide of the tibia on the femur
ar-8ffbb6ae.explanation: The ACL runs from the anterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the inner surface of the lateral femoral condyle; it limits forward slide of the tibia and excessive internal rotation. It is assessed with the anterior drawer and Lachman tests. Backward slide is limited by the PCL, valgus by the medial and varus by the lateral collateral ligament.
notes: This is the role of the medial patellofemoral ligament and VMO.
This is the role of the lateral collateral ligament.
This is the role of the posterior cruciate ligament.
This is the role of the medial collateral ligament.

ar-1653af8f.stem: In a motorcycle accident a patient takes a blow to the front of the upper tibia with the knee bent; with the knee at 90° of flexion the tibia can be pushed backwards relative to the femur. Which ligament is injured?
ar-1653af8f.explanation: The posterior cruciate ligament prevents the tibia sliding backwards; the 'dashboard injury' is the typical mechanism. The posterior drawer test and posterior sag of the tibia (sag sign) are positive. The PCL is thicker and stronger than the ACL.

ar-35c5b540.stem: What are the components of the classic 'unhappy triad' (O'Donoghue) knee injury?
options: Posterior cruciate ligament, lateral collateral ligament and lateral meniscus
Anterior cruciate ligament, posterior cruciate ligament and patellar ligament
Anterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and medial meniscus
Lateral collateral ligament, popliteus tendon and lateral meniscus
Medial collateral ligament, pes anserinus and medial meniscus
ar-35c5b540.explanation: A blow to the outer side of the knee with the foot fixed on the ground tears, through valgus and external rotation, the medial collateral ligament, then the medial meniscus attached to it and the anterior cruciate ligament. Recent studies show that the lateral meniscus is also often involved.
